prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop landing and documentation homepage comp, 1536×1024 landscape
Primary request: create a third compositional option for the Atlas documentation site, preserving the same 1986 Aegean archaeological-terminal visual world but using an architectural section rather than a split hero or constellation map.
Structure: full-width top navigation with ATLAS, GUIDES, PACKAGES, API, GITHUB. The first viewport is organized like a precise plan of a Greek temple excavated by a 1980s computer: a central vertical reading axis with four structural bays. Bay one contains a monumental ATLAS title and the exact statement "Composable, functional Bun/TypeScript building blocks." Bay two is an oversized code slab with exact command "bun add @wess/atlas" and a short real import sample using "@wess/atlas/config", "@wess/atlas/db", and "@wess/atlas/server". Bay three is a scan-friendly index of the 19 packages. Bay four is a guide route with Overview, Quick start, API reference, Cookbook. The outline of Atlas and his celestial sphere appears only as a large halftone registration image crossing the title and code bays, not as a separate poster.
Style/medium: polished shippable documentation website UI. Monumental Greek plan geometry translated into late-1980s scientific desktop publishing: deep Aegean navy, limestone white, electric cyan construction lines, one magenta registration accent, measured Greek-key rules, blueprint coordinates, subtle CRT glow and halftone dots.
Typography: wide chiseled geometric uppercase for ATLAS, humanist sans for prose, narrow mono for technical labels and code.
Composition/framing: full browser viewport with strict axial rhythm and strong reading order; the giant title and integrated Atlas halftone are the one dominant moment; all references remain legible.
Constraints: documentation website, not a poster or museum placard; no rounded bento cards, no generic SaaS hero, no gold luxury aesthetic, no glassmorphism, no invented metrics, customers, package capabilities, or logos, no decorative Greek columns, no watermark, no tiny unreadable text.
